meeting.title: Vector × Modal — implementation kickoff
meeting.summary: Kickoff for the Modal implementation. Agreed an 8-week timeline to go-live with the analytics platform on top of their existing dbt Core project (GitHub, ~140 models on Snowflake). Priya wants self-serve dashboards for engineering leadership first; the AI analyst pilot comes after the semantic layer is trustworthy. Immediate blockers: read-only Snowflake service account and repo access for Vector.
action_items: Erin to provision a read-only Snowflake service account scoped to the ANALYTICS schema by Wednesday
Theo to send the Vector Cloud static IP list for Modal's warehouse network policy
Jonas to grant Vector read access to the dbt repo on GitHub
Maya to share the 8-week implementation plan and weekly sync invite
key_decisions: Go-live target set at 8 weeks from today
Phase 1 audience is engineering leadership dashboards; AI analyst pilot deferred to phase 2
Weekly sync every Tuesday at 4pm CET
meeting.notes: Strong data team — Jonas maintains the dbt project solo and knows it inside out. Erin owns Snowflake and Okta. Priya is the exec sponsor and wants weekly progress visibility.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Thanks everyone for making time. Goal for today is to align on what success looks like and unblock the technical setup so Theo can start this week.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Great. From our side the headline is that engineering leadership is flying blind — every metrics question turns into a notebook someone runs by hand.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That's the exact pattern we see a lot. Can you walk us through the current stack?

transcript.speaker: Jonas Beck
transcript.text: Sure. Everything lands in Snowflake, dbt Core project on GitHub, about a hundred and forty models. CI runs on merge to main. It's healthy — tests pass, docs are decent.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: That's a great starting point. If the project compiles clean we can have the semantic layer scaffolded within days of getting repo access.

transcript.speaker: Erin Castillo
transcript.text: What exactly do you need from the warehouse side?

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: A read-only service account scoped to your ANALYTICS schema, and our static egress IPs added to your network policy. I'll send the IP list right after this call.

transcript.speaker: Erin Castillo
transcript.text: Fine on both. I can have the service account done by Wednesday. Network policy change goes through a quick review but it's routine.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Perfect. Jonas, for the repo — read access for our GitHub app is enough, we never push to your repo.

transcript.speaker: Jonas Beck
transcript.text: Easy, I'll add it today. One question — do you build on top of our existing metrics definitions or do we redefine everything?

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: We read what you have. Where you already have .yml metric definitions we import them; the gaps we fill together in a working session.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: On scope — I want leadership dashboards first. Deployment velocity, GPU utilisation revenue, top customer accounts. The AI analyst thing is exciting but I don't want it answering questions off a semantic layer we don't trust yet.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Completely agree, that's our recommended order anyway. Semantic layer first, dashboards second, AI analyst pilot to a small group once parity is proven.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Then let's say eight weeks to go-live for the dashboard tier. Is that realistic?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: With a project in this shape, yes. The long pole is usually access provisioning, and Erin just volunteered to crush that this week.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Maya will send over the implementation plan and a weekly sync invite — proposing Tuesdays 4pm your time. Any objections?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Great kickoff, everyone. Summary and action items will be in your inbox within the hour.
